correctness.rationale: The deterministic state transition T has spectral norm less than one; its past-innovation series is L² convergent, stationary, and unique by contraction of a synchronously coupled pair. In an orthogonal eigenbasis, conditional on the shared order sequence the stationary coordinates are independent centered Gaussians. Writing a_i=exp(-2h lambda_i), their variances obey the stationary recursion V_i(new)=a_i V_i(old)+2h[a_i+(1-a_i)B] with the same fresh B in all modes. Taking means gives exactly 2h[p+a_i/(1-a_i)], and subtracting 1/lambda_i gives 2h(p-f(h lambda_i)). Strict decrease of f follows from f'(t)=(sinh(t)^(-2)-t^(-2))/2<0; expansions at zero and infinity give its range (0,1/2). The endpoint modes give the maximal absolute error, so equalizing them yields the unique admissible midpoint minimizer, including the isotropic case. For conditional variances the stationary covariance recursion multiplies the old covariance by a_i a_j and adds (2h)^2 (1-a_i)(1-a_j)p(1-p). For distinct orthogonal modes this is also the source of the unconditional square covariance; for a single mode the fourth cumulant is three times the variance of its conditional variance, with (1-a_i)/(1+a_i)=tanh(h lambda_i). Positivity for every interior p precludes a Gaussian stationary law. At p=0,1 the stationary law is Gaussian but f is strictly between those values, so covariance is wrong. The cross-mode result includes repeated eigenvalues with distinct orthogonal coordinates, and is vacuous in dimension one. The small-h expansions and displayed example are consistent with the exact formulas.
residual_risks: Exact rational moment checks and a numerical grid are finite diagnostics. The proof uses contraction and all-parameter identities, not finite sampling or an assumption of independent Bernoulli order across coordinates.

value.rationale: For a standard quadratic test problem this result identifies exactly what a single tunable splitting probability can achieve: the best possible error across all modes and the conditions for zero covariance error. More importantly it gives a sharp obstruction to equating covariance calibration with fidelity of the invariant law, and explains how a common order induces nonlinear dependence despite zero linear cross-covariances. This is useful exact information for evaluating a natural sampler, not a claim that covariance minimization optimizes other metrics.
residual_risks: No inference for nonquadratic targets, other splittings, independent-coordinate choices, or optimization in Wasserstein or total variation.
